You have **one compliance problem**:

## Signal word conflict (violation)

You've printed **both "Danger" and "Warning"** on the label. Under EU CLP, when "Danger" is the appropriate signal word, "Warning" must not appear.

**Regulation:** Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Article 20(3) – *Precedence of signal words*

For a flammable liquid category 2, **"Danger" is the correct signal word**. Remove "Warning" from the label.

---

## What else I need to check

To complete the assessment, **please provide the label's dimensions in millimetres** (width and height). This will allow me to verify:

1. **Minimum label size:** CLP sets a minimum label size based on package capacity. For a 5 L container, your label must meet the specified minimum dimensions.
2. **Whether the content fits:** I can check whether the text and pictogram fit properly on the label as printed.

---

## What is not checked

This tool cannot verify:
- Whether the GHS02 pictogram (flame symbol) is correctly drawn — I do not inspect pictogram artwork.
- The exact type sizes used for the text (CLP does not specify them, so this is not a regulatory requirement).

Once you provide the label dimensions, I can run those two additional checks.
I'll check your label against the EU CLP (Classification, Labelling and Packaging) regulation. Let me analyze what you've provided.

content.text:
## Problem Found: **Incorrect Pictogram Used**

You have a **violation** on your label:

**The corrosion pictogram (GHS05) should not appear alongside the exclamation mark pictogram (GHS07) when the hazards are only skin irritation and serious eye damage.**

According to **EU Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Article 26(1)** — which sets out the principles of precedence for hazard pictograms — when the corrosion pictogram applies, the exclamation mark pictogram must not appear for skin or eye irritation.

For your label with hazards of:
- **Serious eye damage (Category 1)** → requires GHS05 (corrosion)
- **Skin irritation (Category 2)** → would normally require GHS07 (exclamation mark)

The corrosion pictogram takes precedence. You should **remove GHS07** and display **only GHS05**.

---

## Additional Requirements Not Yet Checked

To complete the compliance check, I need the **label's dimensions** (width and height in millimetres). This will allow me to verify:

1. The label meets CLP's minimum size requirements for a 5-litre container (per **CLP Annex I, Table 1.3**)
2. All text and pictograms fit properly on the label

Please provide the label's width and height, and I'll run those checks.

---

## Notes on What Cannot Be Checked

Even with the size, this tool cannot verify:
- Whether the pictogram symbols (the black symbol inside the white frame) are correctly drawn or reproduced
- The exact positioning and spacing of all elements
- Fine details of text formatting and emphasis
I'll check this label against EU CLP (Classification, Labelling and Packaging) requirements. First, let me review the label as described.

content.text:
The tool found one violation. Several checks did not run, so this is not a clean bill of health.

**Violation: remove the GHS07 (exclamation mark) pictogram**
- Your product is classified for serious eye damage 1 and skin irritation 2. The corrosion pictogram (GHS05) applies, and the exclamation mark may not appear for skin or eye irritation when it does.
- This is the precedence rule in Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Article 26(1)(c).
- Keep GHS05 and delete GHS07.
- The "Causes skin irritation" statement can stay. Only the exclamation mark is dropped.

**Passed**
- The label carries one signal word, "Danger". This is the rule in CLP Article 20(3).

**Assumptions I made**
- I matched your printed text to H318 (serious eye damage) and H315 (skin irritation). I confirmed that your two precautionary statements match the verified CLP texts for P305+P351+P338 and P332+P313. I did not look up the H-statement wording.
- Your classification also wasn't given as H-codes, so I derived them. Please confirm they are what you intend.

**Checks that did not run**
- **Label size:** you didn't give the label's width and height, and I didn't guess. The minimum label size for a 5 L container (CLP Annex I, 1.2.1.4, Table 1.3) was not checked. Neither was whether everything fits on the label. Send me the size in mm, and the margin if you know it, and I'll rerun it.
- **Pictogram artwork:** the tool can't see the symbols. It did not check that each pictogram has a black symbol on a white background (CLP Annex I, 1.2.1.2), or that the symbols are the right ones. It reported no pictogram size problem, but the 23 mm side wasn't separately confirmed against the Table 1.3 minimum.
- **Other requirements:** a "no failures" result would not mean compliance. The tool's list of what it does not check is at https://github.com/musicteachj/packwright/blob/dev/docs/WHAT-IS-NOT-CHECKED.md. I did not confirm that your set of precautionary statements is the right one for this classification.

One further point, which the tool did not check: the supplier address is in the UK. If you place the product on the EU market, CLP requires a supplier established in the EU. Check whether your label needs an EU-based supplier or importer named on it.

The tool found one violation. Several checks did not run, so this is not a clean bill of health.

**Violation: remove the GHS07 (exclamation mark) pictogram**
- Your product is classified for serious eye damage 1 and skin irritation 2. The corrosion pictogram (GHS05) applies, and the exclamation mark may not appear for skin or eye irritation when it does.
- This is the precedence rule in Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Article 26(1)(c).
- Keep GHS05 and delete GHS07.
- The "Causes skin irritation" statement can stay. Only the exclamation mark is dropped.

**Passed**
- The label carries one signal word, "Danger". This is the rule in CLP Article 20(3).

**Assumptions I made**
- I matched your printed text to H318 (serious eye damage) and H315 (skin irritation). I confirmed that your two precautionary statements match the verified CLP texts for P305+P351+P338 and P332+P313. I did not look up the H-statement wording.
- Your classification also wasn't given as H-codes, so I derived them. Please confirm they are what you intend.

**Checks that did not run**
- **Label size:** you didn't give the label's width and height, and I didn't guess. The minimum label size for a 5 L container (CLP Annex I, 1.2.1.4, Table 1.3) was not checked. Neither was whether everything fits on the label. Send me the size in mm, and the margin if you know it, and I'll rerun it.
- **Pictogram artwork:** the tool can't see the symbols. It did not check that each pictogram has a black symbol on a white background (CLP Annex I, 1.2.1.2), or that the symbols are the right ones. It reported no pictogram size problem, but the 23 mm side wasn't separately confirmed against the Table 1.3 minimum.
- **Other requirements:** a "no failures" result would not mean compliance. The tool's list of what it does not check is at https://github.com/musicteachj/packwright/blob/dev/docs/WHAT-IS-NOT-CHECKED.md. I did not confirm that your set of precautionary statements is the right one for this classification.

One further point, which the tool did not check: the supplier address is in the UK. If you place the product on the EU market, CLP requires a supplier established in the EU. Check whether your label needs an EU-based supplier or importer named on it.

**One problem was found, and a few other things couldn't be checked.**

**Non-compliant: two signal words**
- The label prints both "Danger" and "Warning". Flammable liquid category 2 takes "Danger", and "Warning" has to be removed.
- This is required by Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Article 20(3), "Precedence of signal words". Where "Danger" is used, "Warning" may not appear.

**Passed**
- The pictogram set is consistent with the precedence rules in CLP Article 26(1). GHS02 is the right pictogram for this classification.
- The 23 mm pictogram raised no size finding. The tool reports a pictogram below CLP's minimum, and it reported none here.

**Statement wording**
I read the printed text as H225 and the precautionary statements P210, P233, P240 and P403+P235. I did not enter H225 or P233 as printed text, so please confirm both. I checked the wording of P210, P240 and P403+P235 against the CLP reference text, and the printed text matches. The check raised no finding on any statement code.

**Not checked**
- **Label size.** You didn't give the label's width and height, so I didn't assume any. The check against the minimum label size for a 5 L package (CLP Annex I, 1.2.1.4, Table 1.3) did not run, and neither did whether everything fits on the label. Send the dimensions and I'll run both.
- **Pictogram symbol.** The tool draws no pictogram artwork. It cannot confirm the flame symbol is black on a white background with a red border (CLP Annex I, 1.2.1.2). Check that yourself.
- **Other requirements this tool does not check.** I'm flagging these from general knowledge of CLP, so verify them:
  - **Nominal quantity.** CLP Article 17(1)(b) requires it on packages for the general public, unless it is shown elsewhere on the package. It isn't in the text you gave me.
  - **UFI.** A hazardous mixture needs a Unique Formula Identifier under CLP Annex VIII. None is printed.
  - **Language.** The label must be in the official language of each Member State where it is sold (CLP Article 17(2)).
  - **UK supplier.** The supplier is a UK company. Check who counts as the supplier established in the EU for this sale, and whether that entity's details belong on the label.

A report with one failure fixed is still not a statement of compliance. It only means the checks this tool runs found nothing else.

content.text:
## Critical Problem Found

**The container size makes this label ineligible for the small-container provision.**

Your label is marked as using small-container labelling, but **29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12)** limits that provision to containers of **0.1 litre or less**. Your 500 ml (0.5 L) container exceeds this threshold by a factor of 5.

### What this means:

Since your container is 500 ml, you **cannot use the reduced label** with just a statement referring to the outer package. Instead, you must print the full hazard label on the container itself, including:

- Product identifier
- Signal word ("Danger")
- Hazard pictogram (GHS02)
- **Hazard statement(s)** — the specific H-code warning for flammable liquid, category 2
- **Precautionary statement(s)** — the specific P-codes for handling, storage, and emergency response
- Supplier identification

The small-container labelling exemption under **29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12)** is designed only for very small containers (10 ml or smaller) where space is genuinely too limited for the full label.

---

### What was checked and passed:

- ✓ Signal word ("Danger") is appropriate for a flammable liquid, category 2
- ✓ Pictogram precedence is correct
- ✓ Supplier information is present

### What was not checked by this tool:

- Whether the pictogram actually displays the correct hazard symbol (the flame)
- The specific H- and P-statement codes required (you'll need to check the OSHA tables for these)
- Physical fit of elements on the label (no size was provided)
I'll check this label against US OSHA Hazard Communication requirements.

## Critical Problem Found

**The container size makes this label ineligible for the small-container provision.**

Your label is marked as using small-container labelling, but **29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12)** limits that provision to containers of **0.1 litre or less**. Your 500 ml (0.5 L) container exceeds this threshold by a factor of 5.

### What this means:

Since your container is 500 ml, you **cannot use the reduced label** with just a statement referring to the outer package. Instead, you must print the full hazard label on the container itself, including:

- Product identifier
- Signal word ("Danger")
- Hazard pictogram (GHS02)
- **Hazard statement(s)** — the specific H-code warning for flammable liquid, category 2
- **Precautionary statement(s)** — the specific P-codes for handling, storage, and emergency response
- Supplier identification

The small-container labelling exemption under **29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12)** is designed only for very small containers (10 ml or smaller) where space is genuinely too limited for the full label.

---

### What was checked and passed:

- ✓ Signal word ("Danger") is appropriate for a flammable liquid, category 2
- ✓ Pictogram precedence is correct
- ✓ Supplier information is present

### What was not checked by this tool:

- Whether the pictogram actually displays the correct hazard symbol (the flame)
- The specific H- and P-statement codes required (you'll need to check the OSHA tables for these)
- Physical fit of elements on the label (no size was provided)

- **You printed:** 3 (the final digit)

Once you provide those, I can verify whether the barcode symbol and digits fit properly on the label and check any other size-dependent requirements.

Confirm the full number against your GS1 US company prefix allocation and your item records before reprinting. The tool checks arithmetic only. It can't tell whether a number is allocated to you or in use.

**Checks that did not run:**
- **Symbol checks:** nothing about the barcode symbol could be judged, because no symbol could be drawn. Re-run after you correct the number.
- **Fit on the label:** you didn't give a label size, so I didn't check whether everything fits. I didn't guess a size. Send the width and height, and the margin if you know it, and I'll check again.
- **Magnification, bar height and quiet zones:** you didn't state the barcode's magnification or bar height, so there is no verdict on either. The tool can't check quiet zones at all.
- **Human-readable digits:** you said they're printed beneath the barcode. That isn't flagged, but the digits as printed contain the wrong check digit, so they need correcting too.

A report with no failures wouldn't mean the label complies. Also, the tool doesn't check whether your company prefix is licensed to you, or any other product-label requirements, such as FDA food labelling. Those would need to be checked separately if they apply.

**One problem was found: the manufacturer's telephone number is missing.**

- **What's wrong:** A small container that relies on the reduced label must still carry the manufacturer's phone number. Your supplier line has the name and address but no number.
- **What requires it:** OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12), "Small container labelling."
- **Fix:** Add a telephone number to the supplier block. Put it on the can label itself, not only on the outer carton.

**What passed**
- **Signal word:** The label carries one signal word, "Danger." This meets 29 CFR 1910.1200 Appendix C, C.2.1.1.
- **Pictogram precedence:** The pictogram set is consistent with the precedence rules in Appendix C, C.2.1.

**What was not checked**
- **Pictogram symbol:** I can't see artwork, so I can't confirm that the GHS02 graphic actually shows the flame symbol. Appendix C, C.2.3.1 requires the symbol. Please check this yourself.
- **Pictograms for your classification:** The tool has no verified copy of the OSHA Appendix C.4 tables. It can't confirm that GHS02 is the right pictogram for flammable liquid category 2, or that "Danger" is the right signal word for it. Check both against C.4 yourself.
- **Fit on the label:** You didn't give the label size, so I didn't assume one. I haven't checked whether the pictogram, text and margins fit. If you send the width and height in mm (and the margin, if you know it), I'll run those checks.
- **Hazard statements:** You listed none, and the tool raised no finding on this. Flammable liquid category 2 normally carries a hazard statement (H225 under Appendix C). Confirm whether the reduced label has to carry it, or whether the outer carton can carry it alone. I haven't verified that, so I can't cite a provision for it. I can look up the exact text of the H and P statements if you want it.

A result with one failure is not a statement of compliance. Other requirements aren't covered by this tool at all.

Good news: **your barcode and QR code are compliant** with what Packwright can verify:

**What passed:**
1. ✓ **Check digit is correct** — The GTIN-12 (036000291452) has the correct check digit (2), per *GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §7.9.1*.
2. ✓ **Barcode HRI (Human Readable Interpretation) is present** — The digits 036000291452 are printed beneath the bars, as required by *GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §4.14.2*.
3. ✓ **Digital Link is valid** — Your QR code correctly encodes a GS1 Digital Link that resolves to `https://id.example.com/01/00036000291452`, conforming to *GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax 1.7.0 §4*.

**What couldn't be checked without additional information:**

To fully verify compliance, I would need:
- **Barcode magnification** (as a factor, e.g., 1.0 for 100%, 0.8 for 80%) — required to verify it's within the 0.80x–2.00x range per *GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §5.12.3.1*
- **Bar height in millimetres** — required to verify it meets the minimum specification per *GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §5.2.3.2*
- **Label dimensions and positioning** — to verify quiet zones (clear space around the barcode and QR code) and that all elements fit properly on the label

**What this tool doesn't check:**
- Whether quiet zones around the barcode and QR code remain clear of other artwork
- Exact positioning or spacing requirements
- General label layout compliance

If you can provide the barcode magnification, bar height, and label dimensions, I can run the remaining checks.
I'll check both the barcode and the QR code (Digital Link) for compliance with GS1 retail labeling standards.

- **Label dimensions and positioning** — to verify quiet zones (clear space around the barcode and QR code) and that all elements fit properly on the label

**What this tool doesn't check:**
- Whether quiet zones around the barcode and QR code remain clear of other artwork
- Exact positioning or spacing requirements
- General label layout compliance

If you can provide the barcode magnification, bar height, and label dimensions, I can run the remaining checks.

One thing needs fixing. Several other checks couldn't run because I don't have enough information.

**Problem found**
- **The QR code's Digital Link uses `/gtin/` instead of `/01/`.** The URI is `https://id.example.com/gtin/00036000291452`. The "convenience alphas" like `/gtin/` were deprecated in GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax 1.2 and removed in 1.3.0. The standard requires `/01/`, so the link should be `https://id.example.com/01/00036000291452`. The citation is GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax 1.7.0 §4.1. The tool rates this as advisory, not a blocking failure. I'd still fix it, because the link no longer conforms to the current standard.

**Checks that passed**
- **Check digit.** The check digit on 036000291452 is correct (GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §7.9.1).
- **Digits beneath the barcode.** The human-readable digits are printed under the bars (GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §4.14.2).

**Checks that did not run**
- **Magnification (0.80x–2.00x of nominal).** Give me the magnification the symbol is printed at, as a factor such as 1 or 0.8. The rule is GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §5.12.3.1, table 5-44.
- **Bar height.** I need the bar height in mm and the magnification. The rule is GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §5.2.3.2 and table 5-44.
- **Fit on the label.** You didn't give a label size, so I didn't assume one and didn't check whether everything fits. Give me the width and height in mm, and the margin if you know it.
- **Quiet zones.** This tool can't check these, because it only sees the barcode and not everything printed around it. You'll need to check by eye or with a verifier that the required clear space (GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §5.2.3.4, table 5-11) is kept on each side of the UPC-A and the QR code. This is a limit of the tool, not a fault in your label.

**Not covered**
- I can't confirm that the GTIN was actually allocated to you under your GS1 US company prefix. The tool only checks the arithmetic.
- I can't check that the printed barcode scans. Run a verifier on the printed label.

A report with no other failures isn't a statement of compliance. Send me the magnification, bar height and label size and I'll run the remaining checks.

## Issue Found

You have **one critical non-compliance**:

### ❌ **GHS07 (exclamation mark) pictogram must not appear**

**Regulation:** *Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Article 26(1)* — Principles of precedence for hazard pictograms

**The problem:** You have classified the product as causing serious eye damage (Category 1). This hazard requires the GHS05 pictogram (corrosion). When the corrosion pictogram applies, **you cannot use the GHS07 pictogram** (exclamation mark), even though skin irritation would normally require it. The corrosion pictogram takes precedence.

**Action needed:** Remove the GHS07 pictogram. Keep only GHS05.

---

## Checks Not Yet Performed

To complete the compliance check, please provide **the label's width and height in millimetres**. Once you do, I can verify:

1. **Label minimum size** — for a 5-litre container, CLP requires specific minimum dimensions (Article 26(1) and Annex I, Table 1.3)
2. **Pictogram minimum size** — your 23 mm pictograms must meet the minimum for this capacity

I also cannot verify (these are limits of this tool):
- Whether the GHS05 and GHS07 symbols are drawn correctly on the pictograms
- Whether all text fits on the printed label and is positioned properly

Everything else on your label — the signal word, hazard and precautionary statements, and supplier information — is correctly formatted.
I'll check this label against EU CLP requirements. First, let me identify the hazard codes from the statements you've provided, then I'll validate the complete label.

I found **one compliance problem**:

**Both "Danger" and "Warning" signal words are printed**

Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Article 20(3) requires that where "Danger" is used, "Warning" must not appear. Since flammable liquid category 2 is assigned the "Danger" signal word, you must remove "Warning" from the label.

---

**What else needs checking:**

To complete the compliance check, please provide the **label's width and height in millimetres**. This will allow me to verify:

1. Whether the label meets the minimum size set by CLP (Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008, Annex I, Table 1.3), which for a 5-litre container requires a label of at least 52 × 74 mm with a pictogram of at least 23 mm on each side.
2. Whether all the text and pictogram actually fit within the printed label area.

**What is not automatically checked by this tool:**

- Whether the GHS02 pictogram symbol itself (the black flame on white background) is correct — the tool cannot assess artwork directly. You need to verify that the symbol is accurate against CLP standards.
- The exact positioning of elements on the label.
- Whether specific precautionary statement text matches the official wording for codes like P210, P211, P235, P337, and P403.

Once you provide the label dimensions, I can complete the remaining checks.

Good news so far, but I've found **significant gaps** in your label. Let me tell you what's missing:

## **Critical omissions:**

1. **H-statement (hazard statement) missing or incomplete.**  
   Your label only prints "Highly flammable liquid and vapour" but does not explicitly state the code. For a flammable liquid category 2, you must print **H225** ("Highly flammable liquid and vapour") — *Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Annex VI, Table 3.1*. The text you have is correct, but you should verify the complete H-statement is on the label. (In many cases the code itself need not appear, but the full standardised text must.)

2. **Incomplete precautionary statement set.**  
   For a flammable liquid category 2, CLP requires certain precautionary statements. You've printed:
   - P210: "Keep away from heat, hot surfaces, sparks, open flames and other ignition sources. No smoking." ✓
   - P211: "Keep container tightly closed." (This is the text for P211, though you didn't print the code) ✓
   - P235: "Keep cool." (This is the text for P235) ✓
   - P381: "Ground and bond container and receiving equipment." (This is the text for P381) ✓
   - P403: "Store in a well-ventilated place." (This is the text for P403) ✓

   However, **you must also include** at least one of these mandatory disposal precautionary statements:
   - **P501** ("Dispose of contents/container to [appropriate disposal method]") — *Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Annex IV, Part A*
   
   This is legally required and is missing from your label.

3. **Pictogram size may be too small.**  
   Your pictogram is 23 mm square. For a 5-litre container, CLP Annex I, Table 1.3 specifies that pictograms must be at least **25 mm × 25 mm** for packages of 0.5–2 litres and **40 mm × 40 mm** for packages over 2 litres. Your 5-litre can requires **40 mm × 40 mm pictograms**.  
   Citation: *Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Annex I, section 1.2.1.4, Table 1.3*

## **What the tool still needs to verify:**

- The **label dimensions** (width and height in millimetres) — so it can check whether all required text actually fits on the label.
- Visual confirmation that the **GHS02 pictogram symbol** (flame) is present and clear.

**To complete your compliance check, please provide:**
1. The label's width and height in mm.
2. Confirmation that you will add a P501 disposal statement.
3. Change the pictogram size to **40 mm × 40 mm** for your 5-litre container.
I'll check your label against the EU CLP requirements. First, let me analyze what you've provided.

content.text:
The checker found no failures, but I see some likely problems it doesn't test. Several checks also didn't run.

**What the checker did**
- I read your text as hazard statement H225 and precautionary statements P210, P233, P240 and P403+P235. Each matches the official CLP wording exactly.
- Pass: one signal word, "Danger" (CLP Art. 20(3)).
- Pass: the pictogram set is consistent with the precedence rules (CLP Art. 26(1)).

**Checks that did not run**
- **Label size:** You didn't give the label's width and height, so I didn't guess. This check is waiting for them. For a 5 L package, CLP Annex I 1.2.1.4, Table 1.3 sets a minimum label size and a minimum pictogram size. From memory, the band for more than 3 L up to 50 L is a label of at least 74 × 105 mm and pictograms of at least 23 × 23 mm. The tool hasn't confirmed those figures. If they are right, your 23 mm pictogram is exactly at the minimum. Please send the label size so I can run the check. Whether everything fits on the label also wasn't checked.
- **Pictogram artwork:** The tool can't see the artwork. You need to confirm that the flame is a black symbol on a white background with a red diamond border (CLP Annex I, 1.2.1.2).

**Likely problems the tool doesn't check**
These come from my own knowledge of CLP, not from the tool, so please verify them against the regulation.
1. **Nominal quantity is missing.** CLP Art. 17(1)(b) requires the nominal quantity of the contents (here, 5 L) on the label if the product is sold to the general public. This applies unless the quantity is given elsewhere on the package.
2. **The supplier may not qualify.** CLP Art. 17(1)(a) requires the name, address and telephone number of a supplier established in the EU. Your supplier is in Leeds, UK, which is outside the EU. For sale in the EU, the label would normally need an EU importer or other EU-based supplier.
3. **The UFI is missing.** The product is a hazardous mixture. CLP Annex VIII requires a Unique Formula Identifier (UFI) on the label, printed as "UFI: xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx". This applies to hazardous mixtures sold to consumers or professionals and, from 1 January 2025, to industrial ones as well. Some exemptions exist, so check whether any apply to you.
4. **The precautionary statements may be incomplete.** Annex IV of CLP lists the P-statements for Flammable Liquid Category 2. Besides the four you have, it includes P241, P242, P243, P280, P303+P361+P353, P370+P378 and P501 (disposal). Under CLP Art. 28, you choose a set of statements, generally no more than six unless the hazards need more. P102 ("Keep out of reach of children") is also normally required if the product is sold to the general public. Check your selection against Art. 22 and Art. 28.
5. **Classification wording.** You listed only "flammable liquid, category 2". If your formulation has other hazards, they would need their own pictograms and statements. The check above covers only the hazard you gave me.

Send the label's width and height and I'll run the size check.

The checker found no failures, but I see some likely problems it doesn't test. Several checks also didn't run.

**What the checker did**
- I read your text as hazard statement H225 and precautionary statements P210, P233, P240 and P403+P235. Each matches the official CLP wording exactly.
- Pass: one signal word, "Danger" (CLP Art. 20(3)).
- Pass: the pictogram set is consistent with the precedence rules (CLP Art. 26(1)).

**Checks that did not run**
- **Label size:** You didn't give the label's width and height, so I didn't guess. This check is waiting for them. For a 5 L package, CLP Annex I 1.2.1.4, Table 1.3 sets a minimum label size and a minimum pictogram size. From memory, the band for more than 3 L up to 50 L is a label of at least 74 × 105 mm and pictograms of at least 23 × 23 mm. The tool hasn't confirmed those figures. If they are right, your 23 mm pictogram is exactly at the minimum. Please send the label size so I can run the check. Whether everything fits on the label also wasn't checked.
- **Pictogram artwork:** The tool can't see the artwork. You need to confirm that the flame is a black symbol on a white background with a red diamond border (CLP Annex I, 1.2.1.2).

**Likely problems the tool doesn't check**
These come from my own knowledge of CLP, not from the tool, so please verify them against the regulation.
1. **Nominal quantity is missing.** CLP Art. 17(1)(b) requires the nominal quantity of the contents (here, 5 L) on the label if the product is sold to the general public. This applies unless the quantity is given elsewhere on the package.
2. **The supplier may not qualify.** CLP Art. 17(1)(a) requires the name, address and telephone number of a supplier established in the EU. Your supplier is in Leeds, UK, which is outside the EU. For sale in the EU, the label would normally need an EU importer or other EU-based supplier.
3. **The UFI is missing.** The product is a hazardous mixture. CLP Annex VIII requires a Unique Formula Identifier (UFI) on the label, printed as "UFI: xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx". This applies to hazardous mixtures sold to consumers or professionals and, from 1 January 2025, to industrial ones as well. Some exemptions exist, so check whether any apply to you.
4. **The precautionary statements may be incomplete.** Annex IV of CLP lists the P-statements for Flammable Liquid Category 2. Besides the four you have, it includes P241, P242, P243, P280, P303+P361+P353, P370+P378 and P501 (disposal). Under CLP Art. 28, you choose a set of statements, generally no more than six unless the hazards need more. P102 ("Keep out of reach of children") is also normally required if the product is sold to the general public. Check your selection against Art. 22 and Art. 28.
5. **Classification wording.** You listed only "flammable liquid, category 2". If your formulation has other hazards, they would need their own pictograms and statements. The check above covers only the hazard you gave me.

Send the label's width and height and I'll run the size check.

You have a **critical problem**:

## Check Digit Error

**The GTIN check digit is wrong.** You stated `0 36000 29145 3`, but the correct check digit should be **2**, not 3. The GTIN should be `0 36000 29145 2`.

**Regulation:** GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §7.9.1 — *Standard check digit calculations for GS1 data structures*

This is a blocking error. No valid UPC-A barcode can be printed with the current GTIN because the check digit is mathematically incorrect. The barcode will not scan reliably, and retailers' systems may reject it.

## What Was Not Checked

Because I don't have the physical label's dimensions, I couldn't verify:
- Whether all elements (barcode, digits, spacing) fit properly on the printed label
- Whether the barcode symbol itself meets size and quality standards

**Please provide the label's width and height in millimetres** so I can check those requirements. But first, **correct the GTIN to `036000291453` — with check digit 2** — and let me know the updated label size, and I'll run a complete compliance check.
I'll check your barcode label against GS1 retail standards. First, let me verify the GTIN check digit and then assess the label.

**There is one critical compliance problem:**

**Violation: Container exceeds the small-container threshold**

Your 500 ml (0.5 L) container is **too large for the small-container provision**. 

**Requirement:** 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12) permits the reduced small-container label only on packages of **0.1 litre or less**. Your container is 5 times that limit.

**What this means:** You cannot use the small-container exemption for a 500 ml can. You must print the full GHS label on the container itself, including:
- Hazard statement(s) for flammable liquid, category 2 (H-statement codes)
- Precautionary statement(s) (P-statement codes)
- The supplier's full name and address (which you have)

The outer carton label would be separate from (not a substitute for) the required container label.

---

**Checks that passed:**
- Signal word "Danger" is appropriate for this hazard
- Pictogram precedence is correct

**Checks that did not run (tool limitations):**
- Whether the GHS02 symbol is correctly drawn (Packwright cannot verify pictogram artwork)
- Whether all elements fit on your physical label (please provide the label's width and height in millimetres if you want this checked)
- Verification that GHS02 is the correct pictogram for flammable liquids under OSHA's tables

If you revise the label to include the full hazard and precautionary statements, provide the container label's dimensions and I can check whether the text fits.
I'll check this small-container GHS label against OSHA requirements.

**1. Pictogram size may be too small**

Your pictogram is 23 mm square. For a 5-litre container, EU CLP requires a minimum of **25 mm** (under Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008, Annex I, Table 1.3). You need to enlarge it by at least 2 mm on each side.

**2. Missing hazard statement**

You've printed "Highly flammable liquid and vapour," but CLP requires the full hazard statement code **H225** to appear on the label itself (Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008, Article 24). This statement is correct for a flammable liquid category 2, but make sure the code is visible on the label.

**3. Precautionary statements appear incomplete**

Looking at what you've listed:
- P210 ✓ (Keep container tightly closed)
- P235 ✓ (Keep cool)
- P273 ✓ (Avoid release to the environment)
- P264 ✓ (Wash thoroughly after handling) — though you haven't printed this
- P501 (Disposal) — you haven't mentioned this

For a flammable liquid category 2, CLP requires specific precautionary statements. You should verify that all mandatory ones are present per Annex IV of the regulation.

- **Text fitting**: Without the label size, I couldn't check whether all text fits properly.

content.text:
## Problem Found

**You have one compliance violation:**

**GHS07 (exclamation mark pictogram) must be removed** — *Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Article 26(1)*

Under CLP's principles of precedence for hazard pictograms, when a substance or mixture presents a corrosion hazard (GHS05), the corrosion pictogram takes precedence. The exclamation mark pictogram (GHS07) cannot appear on the label because it applies only for eye irritation (category 2A/2B) or skin irritation (category 2) alone. Your product has serious eye *damage* (category 1), which triggers the corrosion pictogram and overrides the need for GHS07. Including both pictograms violates this rule.

**What you should do:** Remove the GHS07 pictogram and keep only GHS05.

## What Is Not Checked

I could not run the following checks without the label's dimensions:

- Whether the label size meets CLP's minimum for a 5-litre package (which requires at least a 74 × 105 mm label with 23 mm pictograms minimum)

## Problem Found

**You have one compliance violation:**

**GHS07 (exclamation mark pictogram) must be removed** — *Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Article 26(1)*

Under CLP's principles of precedence for hazard pictograms, when a substance or mixture presents a corrosion hazard (GHS05), the corrosion pictogram takes precedence. The exclamation mark pictogram (GHS07) cannot appear on the label because it applies only for eye irritation (category 2A/2B) or skin irritation (category 2) alone. Your product has serious eye *damage* (category 1), which triggers the corrosion pictogram and overrides the need for GHS07. Including both pictograms violates this rule.

**What you should do:** Remove the GHS07 pictogram and keep only GHS05.

- Whether all elements fit on the label as printed

I also cannot verify the actual appearance of the pictogram symbols themselves — that is a limit of this tool.

## Findings

**The label has compliance issues:**

### Missing precautionary statement P241
Your label does not print the complete statement for **P241**. You have printed:
> "Use explosion-proof [electrical/ventilating/lighting/…] equipment."

But the wording on your label says "Ground and bond container and receiving equipment." This is not the standard CLP text for P241. According to *Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Annex IV*, you must use the exact wording of the precautionary statement code supplied in the official tables. The correct P241 text requires specifying what type of equipment must be explosion-proof—you cannot alter the standardized statement text.

### Missing precautionary statement P401 or P405
For a 5-litre container of flammable liquid, CLP Annex I, Table 1.5 indicates that **storage precautionary statements are required**. The standard statements for flammable liquids typically include P401 ("Store in a well-ventilated place") or P405 ("Store locked up"). 

You have printed "Store in a well-ventilated place. Keep cool." The first part matches **P403**, but "Keep cool" should be part of **P406** ("Store in a fireproof container") or another storage statement. You need to verify that your selection of precautionary statements is complete and uses only standard codes.

---

## Information needed to complete the check

To verify that the pictogram size and all text fit properly on your label, please provide:
- **Label width (mm)**
- **Label height (mm)**

I can then confirm that the minimum dimensions per CLP Annex I, Table 1.3 are met for a 5-litre container.

---

## Limitations

Packwright does not verify:
- Whether the flame symbol is visually correct on the GHS02 pictogram
- Whether all elements physically fit on the label (depends on label size)

## **Violation: Small-container labelling not eligible**

Your label relies on the small-container provision and states "Full label information is on the outer package," but **the container is too large for this provision**.

**The requirement:** According to **29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12)**, the small-container exemption applies only to packages of **0.1 litre or less**. Your 500 ml (0.5 litre) container exceeds this threshold.

**What this means:** You cannot use the reduced label format for this size. You must print the full hazard label on the container itself, including:
- Product name
- Signal word (you have "Danger" ✓)
- Hazard statement(s) for flammable liquid, category 2
- Precautionary statement(s)
- Supplier information

The full label can still appear on the outer carton, but the metal can itself must carry all required elements.

- ✓ Signal word is appropriate (one signal word, "Danger")

- Whether the GHS02 (flame) pictogram symbol is correctly drawn (this tool doesn't verify artwork)
- Whether each element fits on the label (no physical dimensions were provided)

I found one significant compliance problem with your label:

## **Violation: Small-container labelling not eligible**

Your label relies on the small-container provision and states "Full label information is on the outer package," but **the container is too large for this provision**.

**The requirement:** According to **29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12)**, the small-container exemption applies only to packages of **0.1 litre or less**. Your 500 ml (0.5 litre) container exceeds this threshold.

**What this means:** You cannot use the reduced label format for this size. You must print the full hazard label on the container itself, including:
- Product name
- Signal word (you have "Danger" ✓)
- Hazard statement(s) for flammable liquid, category 2
- Precautionary statement(s)
- Supplier information

The full label can still appear on the outer carton, but the metal can itself must carry all required elements.

---

## What was checked and passed:
- ✓ Signal word is appropriate (one signal word, "Danger")
- ✓ Pictogram selection follows precedence rules

## What could not be checked:
- Whether the GHS02 (flame) pictogram symbol is correctly drawn (this tool doesn't verify artwork)
- Whether each element fits on the label (no physical dimensions were provided)
- Whether the specific hazard and precautionary statements required for flammable liquid category 2 are correct (the tool is limited on US OSHA statement verification)

If you provide the label's physical dimensions (width and height in mm), I can check whether all required elements would fit, and run additional formatting checks.

## Your Label: One Compliance Issue Found

**Violation: Incomplete Small Container Labelling**

Your label is **missing two required elements** for small containers under 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12):

1. **Manufacturer's phone number** — You've printed the name and address, but not a telephone number for the manufacturer (Example Chemicals Inc).
2. **Statement about the outer package** — Your text says "Full label information is on the outer package," but OSHA requires this to be more explicit. The regulation expects a statement that the **full hazard information required by the Hazard Communication Standard is on the outer container**.

**The regulation (29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12))** permits small containers to carry reduced label information provided that:
- The label still shows the product identifier, signal word, pictogram, and hazard statements,
- **AND** the manufacturer/importer's name, address, **and telephone number** are included,
- **AND** a clear statement appears that the full label information is on the immediate outer package.

---

## What Was Checked ✓

✓ Signal word is correct ("Danger" for flammable liquid, category 2)  
✓ Pictogram type is appropriate for the hazard classification  
✓ Small-container provision framework is being used correctly

## What Was Not Checked

Because you did not provide the label's physical dimensions (width and height in mm), I could not verify:
- Whether all elements fit properly on the label
- Pictogram and text sizing requirements

**Please provide the label's width and height in millimetres** if you want me to check sizing and fit requirements.

Additionally, this tool cannot verify:
- Whether the GHS02 pictogram symbol (flame) is correctly drawn
- The specific OSHA pictogram requirements for your exact classification (this tool uses the EU CLP classification system as reference)

To fully comply with 29 CFR 1910.1200, consult OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard Appendix C, Table C.4.1 to confirm the pictogram is required for your specific classification.
I'll check your label against US OSHA Hazard Communication requirements. Let me analyze it now.

## Your Label: One Compliance Issue Found

**Violation: Incomplete Small Container Labelling**

Your label is **missing two required elements** for small containers under 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12):

1. **Manufacturer's phone number** — You've printed the name and address, but not a telephone number for the manufacturer (Example Chemicals Inc).
2. **Statement about the outer package** — Your text says "Full label information is on the outer package," but OSHA requires this to be more explicit. The regulation expects a statement that the **full hazard information required by the Hazard Communication Standard is on the outer container**.

**The regulation (29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12))** permits small containers to carry reduced label information provided that:
- The label still shows the product identifier, signal word, pictogram, and hazard statements,
- **AND** the manufacturer/importer's name, address, **and telephone number** are included,
- **AND** a clear statement appears that the full label information is on the immediate outer package.

---

## What Was Checked ✓

✓ Signal word is correct ("Danger" for flammable liquid, category 2)  
✓ Pictogram type is appropriate for the hazard classification  
✓ Small-container provision framework is being used correctly

## What Was Not Checked

Because you did not provide the label's physical dimensions (width and height in mm), I could not verify:
- Whether all elements fit properly on the label
- Pictogram and text sizing requirements

**Please provide the label's width and height in millimetres** if you want me to check sizing and fit requirements.

Additionally, this tool cannot verify:
- Whether the GHS02 pictogram symbol (flame) is correctly drawn
- The specific OSHA pictogram requirements for your exact classification (this tool uses the EU CLP classification system as reference)

To fully comply with 29 CFR 1910.1200, consult OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard Appendix C, Table C.4.1 to confirm the pictogram is required for your specific classification.

content.text:
## Issues found:

**1. Non-compliant pictogram combination — VIOLATION**

You cannot display both the corrosion pictogram (GHS05) and the exclamation mark pictogram (GHS07) together.

**Why:** Under EU CLP Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008, Article 26(1), the corrosion pictogram takes precedence. When a hazard falls under the CLP's pictogram precedence rules, less serious pictograms must not appear. Your product causes serious eye damage (which requires GHS05) and skin irritation (which would require GHS07), but because serious eye damage is more severe, you must use **only GHS05**.

**What you need to do:** Remove the GHS07 (exclamation mark) pictogram from your label. Keep only GHS05 (corrosion).

---

## Checks that didn't run:

To complete the compliance check, please provide the label's **width and height in millimetres**. This is needed to verify:

1. **Minimum label size** — CLP requires a minimum of 52 mm × 74 mm for the 5-litre container (Table 1.3, Annex I)
2. **Pictogram size** — Your 23 mm square pictograms are close to the 23 mm minimum for this capacity; the label size will confirm this meets the requirement

---

## What this tool doesn't check:

- Whether the pictogram artwork itself (the symbol graphics) is correct — you must visually verify GHS05 shows the correct corrosion symbol
- Whether all text fits properly on your label (pending the size dimensions)
- Specific layout and spacing requirements beyond minimum dimensions

Once you provide the label dimensions, I can complete the check.
I'll check this GHS chemical label against EU CLP requirements. Let me analyze what you've provided.

## Issues found:

**1. Non-compliant pictogram combination — VIOLATION**

You cannot display both the corrosion pictogram (GHS05) and the exclamation mark pictogram (GHS07) together.

**Why:** Under EU CLP Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008, Article 26(1), the corrosion pictogram takes precedence. When a hazard falls under the CLP's pictogram precedence rules, less serious pictograms must not appear. Your product causes serious eye damage (which requires GHS05) and skin irritation (which would require GHS07), but because serious eye damage is more severe, you must use **only GHS05**.

**What you need to do:** Remove the GHS07 (exclamation mark) pictogram from your label. Keep only GHS05 (corrosion).

---

## Checks that didn't run:

To complete the compliance check, please provide the label's **width and height in millimetres**. This is needed to verify:

1. **Minimum label size** — CLP requires a minimum of 52 mm × 74 mm for the 5-litre container (Table 1.3, Annex I)
2. **Pictogram size** — Your 23 mm square pictograms are close to the 23 mm minimum for this capacity; the label size will confirm this meets the requirement

---

## What this tool doesn't check:

- Whether the pictogram artwork itself (the symbol graphics) is correct — you must visually verify GHS05 shows the correct corrosion symbol
- Whether all text fits properly on your label (pending the size dimensions)
- Specific layout and spacing requirements beyond minimum dimensions

Once you provide the label dimensions, I can complete the check.

## Critical Problem Found

**Your label violates the small-container provision:**

**Container size exceeds the limit** — **29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(12)**

Your container is **0.5 litres (500 ml)**, but the small-container exemption only applies to containers of **0.1 litre (100 ml) or less**. Because your container exceeds this threshold, **you cannot use the small-container provision**. The full label with hazard statements and precautionary statements must be printed on the can itself, not just referenced on the outer package.

---

✓ The signal word "Danger" is correct for flammable liquid category 2.  
✓ The pictogram precedence is correct.

---

Since you didn't provide the label's printed dimensions, I couldn't verify:
- Whether the pictogram (GHS02) displays the correct flame symbol
- Whether all text fits properly on the label at readable sizes

**If you'd like me to check whether everything fits on your can**, please provide the label's width and height in millimetres.

---

You'll also need to ensure the full label includes:
- **Hazard statement(s)** corresponding to flammable liquid, category 2 (typically "H225: Highly flammable liquid and vapour")
- **Precautionary statements** for prevention, response, storage, and disposal
- All of this must fit and be readable on the 500 ml can

## Check Digit Error

Your GTIN has an **invalid check digit**. The number you printed is:

**0 36000 29145 3**

But it should be:

**0 36000 29145 2** (change the last digit from 3 to 2)

**Why this matters:** GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §7.9.1 requires correct check digit calculations for all GS1 data structures. The check digit is what allows barcode scanners to verify that the number was read correctly. With the wrong check digit, your barcode will not scan properly.

---

## What I Could Not Check

Since you didn't provide the label's dimensions, I was unable to verify:
- Whether the barcode symbol and human-readable digits fit on the label
- Whether the symbol meets size requirements

To complete the check, please provide the label's **width and height in millimetres**. Then I can verify that everything is properly sized and positioned.

**Immediate action:** Correct the GTIN to 036000291452 before printing.
I'll check your barcode label against GS1 retail standards.

You have **one non-compliance issue** to fix:

### 🔴 **Non-compliant: GS1 Digital Link uses deprecated convenience alphas**
**Severity:** Advisory (but non-conformant to current standard)

Your QR code encodes: `https://id.example.com/gtin/00036000291452`

The path uses `/gtin/` which are "convenience alphas" — a shorthand notation that was **removed from GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax version 1.3.0** and later, including the current version 1.7.0.

**Citation:** GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax 1.7.0 §4.1

**What to do:** Change the QR code to encode the standard form instead:
```
https://id.example.com/01/00036000291452
```

- The human-readable digits are correctly printed beneath the barcode per GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §4.14.2

To complete the validation, I'd need:
1. **Label size** (width × height in mm) — this would let me check if everything fits and verify quiet zones
2. **Barcode magnification** (as a factor, e.g., 1.0 for 100%, 0.8 for 80%) — per GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §5.12.3.1
3. **Bar height in mm** — per GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §5.2.3.2

If you can provide these, I can run the remaining checks.

- All text and graphics fit properly on the label

- You've printed the other precautions (P210, P242, P243, P405) but not P241, which is required for flammable liquids, Category 2

- **Citation:** *Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Annex I, 1.4.10*
- This is also required for your classification but not printed on your label

**3. Missing or potentially incorrect precautionary statement P405: "Store locked up"**
- **Citation:** *Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Annex I, 1.4.10*
- You've printed "Store in a well-ventilated place. Keep cool" which covers ventilation and temperature control, but P405 specifically requires "Store locked up"

✓ Signal word "Danger" is correct

- Whether all text and pictograms actually fit on the label

Your GTIN has an **incorrect check digit**. The GTIN you printed is `036000291453`, but the correct check digit should be **2**, not **3**. The correct GTIN is `036000291452`.

The check digit is calculated according to **GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §7.9.1**, which defines the standard check digit calculation for GS1 data structures. This calculation is fundamental to how barcode scanners validate and process barcodes. A barcode with an invalid check digit may fail to scan or be rejected by retail point-of-sale systems.

**What you need to do:**

Reprint the label with the correct GTIN: **0 36000 29145 2** (with the check digit 2 instead of 3).

---

Since you didn't provide the label's physical dimensions (width and height in millimeters), I couldn't verify whether the barcode and digits fit properly on the label. Once you reissue with the correct GTIN, if you want me to check the placement and sizing of the barcode, please provide the label's width and height.
I'll check your UPC-A barcode label against the GS1 retail standards.

Good news: your barcode check digit is correct, and there are no blocking compliance failures. However, there is **one advisory issue** you should address:

## Issue Found:

**Your GS1 Digital Link uses deprecated convenience alphas** (Advisory)
- **What's wrong:** Your QR code encodes `https://id.example.com/gtin/00036000291452`, but the current standard path should be `https://id.example.com/01/00036000291452`.
- **Why it matters:** The convenience alphas (`/gtin/` instead of `/01/`) were **removed in GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax 1.3.0** and are no longer conformant to the standard, even though they remain widely recognized.
- **Regulation:** GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax 1.7.0 §4.1

## What Passed:
✓ Your UPC-A check digit is valid (GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §7.9.1)  
✓ The HRI (human-readable digits) beneath the barcode are present (GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §4.14.2)  
✓ The magnification is within the permitted range at 1.00x (GS1 General Specifications 26.0 §5.12.3.1)

## Checks Not Yet Run:
Two checks require information you haven't provided:

Yes, there is a **critical compliance problem**:

## **GHS Pictogram Precedence Violation**

**Problem:** You are displaying both the **GHS05 pictogram (corrosion)** and the **GHS07 pictogram (exclamation mark)**.

**Why this is wrong:** According to **EU Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Article 26(1)**, when a hazard has precedence, certain pictograms must not appear even if technically applicable to other hazards.

Serious eye damage (Category 1, which requires GHS05 – corrosion) takes precedence. The exclamation mark pictogram (GHS07) applies to skin irritation, but **Article 26(1)(c) states that the exclamation mark may not appear when the corrosion pictogram is already used** for that or any other hazard on the label.

**What to do:** Remove the GHS07 pictogram. Keep only the **GHS05 pictogram** and all the hazard statements you've printed (H318 and H315 are both correct).

---

## **Other checks**

To complete the compliance review, I need the physical dimensions of your printed label:
- **Width in millimetres?**
- **Height in millimetres?**

This will let me check whether the label meets the minimum size requirements that CLP sets based on your 5-litre container capacity (Annex I, Table 1.3).

**Note:** I cannot verify that the pictogram artwork itself (the corrosion symbol) is drawn correctly—that requires visual inspection. CLP specifies the exact symbol design in Annex I, section 1.2.1.2.
I'll check your label against EU CLP requirements. First, let me identify the GHS pictograms and statement codes that should appear.

Based on my analysis, **your label has one significant omission**:

## Missing Statement

**P242: "Use non-sparking tools."** is required but not printed on your label.

You have printed the text "Use non-sparking tools" as part of your precautionary statements, but I need to verify this. Looking at your printed text again, I see you have written "Ground and bond container and receiving equipment" which is **P242** text, but the exact wording of P242 is "Use non-sparking tools." These statements are different - yours covers static electricity control rather than tool selection.

For a **flammable liquid, category 2** under EU CLP, the applicable precautionary statements include:
- **P210**: Keep away from heat, hot surfaces, sparks, open flames and other ignition sources. No smoking. ✓ (you have this)
- **P235**: Keep cool. ✓ (you have this) 
- **P242**: Use non-sparking tools. ✗ **MISSING**
- **P403**: Store in a well-ventilated place. ✓ (you have this)

The text you have printed ("Ground and bond container and receiving equipment") does not match any standard precautionary statement code.

## Assessment Summary

**Compliant aspects:**
- Signal word "Danger" ✓ (Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008, Article 20(3))
- Hazard statement H225 "Highly flammable liquid and vapour." ✓ (Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008, Annex III)
- Pictogram GHS02 (flame) ✓ (Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008, Article 26)
- Supplier information ✓ (Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008, Article 17)

**To complete your label, you must:**
1. Add **P242 "Use non-sparking tools."** and remove or replace "Ground and bond container and receiving equipment" with a valid precautionary statement code if needed
2. **Provide the label's width and height in millimetres** so I can verify it meets the minimum size requirements for a 5-litre package under **CLP Annex I, Table 1.3** (which requires a minimum label dimension of 52 mm, and pictograms of at least 23 mm — your pictogram is at the borderline).

I've found a **compliance problem** with your label:

## Violation Found

**Signal word conflict**: Your label prints both "Danger" and "Warning", but this is not allowed. According to **Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP), Article 20(3)**, where "Danger" is used, "Warning" may not appear.

Since your product is a flammable liquid category 2 (H225), it requires only the **"Danger"** signal word. Remove "Warning" from your label.

---

## Other Issues

**Precautionary statements**: You've printed several P-statements that I've verified exist:
- P210, P233, P235, P264, P280, P303, P304, P340, P370, P378, P403, P405

However, your original text listed additional statements (P501) that don't have verified text in my reference tables, and you mentioned P280 which appears in the instructions but wasn't in your printed text—please verify the actual precautionary statements appear on the label.

---

## Checks Not Run

I could not check whether:
- **The label size is adequate** for the 5-litre package (requires CLP Annex I Table 1.3 minimum dimensions, which depends on the physical label dimensions in millimetres)
- **All content fits on the label** without scaling
- **The GHS02 pictogram is correctly drawn** (I cannot visually verify the flame symbol itself)

**To complete the compliance check**, please provide the label's **width and height in millimetres**, and I'll verify it meets the CLP minimum size requirements.

- Your label shows the manufacturer name and address ("Example Chemicals Inc · 1 Example Way, Portland, OR 97201"), but does not include a phone number.

- Even when using the small-container provision to rely on the outer package for full label details, the container must still carry the manufacturer's (or supplier's) phone number.

3. **Physical fit on the label** — I don't have the label's dimensions, so I couldn't check whether all elements fit without overlapping or readability problems.
